question: In the reactor network of the staged-air pulverized-coal boiler co-firing ammonia, which reactor receives the overfire air, and what is its role?
expect: C1-R5, Burnout Zone (OFA): further oxidation with overfire air, char burnout; inlets from R4 + OFA (Table 1)
trap: C1-R3 (70% secondary air) or C1-R4 reduction zone
rendered:
Based on the provided text, the reactor network of the 350 MW pulverized-coal boiler with staged air is as follows:

C1-R1: Mixing Zone - receives primary air, coal, and 20% FGR (flue gas recirculation)
C1-R2: Flame Zone - receives main ignition/heat release from R1 and 30% Secondary air
C1-R3: Post Flame Zone - receives further oxidation and heat release from R2 and 70% Secondary air
C1-R4: Reduction Zone - receives NO reduction/char reactions from R3
C1-R5: Burnout Zone (OFA) - receives further oxidation with overfire air from R4
C1-R6: Downstream Section-1 - receives gas cooling/cleanup from R5
C1-R7: Recirculation Zone - provides FGR to R1/R2
C1-R8: Downstream Section-2(Exit) - furnace exit composition from R6

The reactor that receives the overfire air is C1-R5: Burnout Zone (OFA). Its role is to provide further oxidation with overfire air to the char, allowing for its complete burnout.
